first_impression.reaction: Sophie sent me this, so I read it properly on the iPad. The opening is calm and sensible, not gushing. I liked that it promises to say which stories are true and which aren't. I can't stand being told nonsense with confidence.

journey.quote: This guide sets out where each tradition really comes from, using museum, encyclopaedia and church sources, and flags the stories that do not hold up.
journey.reaction: Good. Museums and the church, not someone on Instagram. That's a grown-up way to write.

journey.quote: Smartraveller advises speaking to a lawyer to confirm validity.
journey.reaction: This is what my husband will ask about first: is the marriage actually legal? Pointing us to the government site and a lawyer, rather than waving it away, makes me trust them more.

journey.quote: So many couples complete the legal marriage at home and give the ceremony abroad all the meaning. Your Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements for your destination.
journey.reaction: Sensible, and there's a person who checks it. I'd still want to know who that person is and how I reach them, but this is a start.

journey.quote: House rules like these are rarely published, so your Wedded Advisor confirms them with the venue in writing.
journey.reaction: 'In writing' is the phrase I was looking for. It comes up again with the confetti and the fire too. Whoever wrote this knows that verbal promises from an overseas venue are worth nothing.

journey.section: Giving away and walking down the aisle
journey.quote: It allows the father, mother or another family member or friend to present the bride.
journey.reaction: Well, that's nice to read. Nobody ever assumes the mother might do it. I'll show this to Sophie.

journey.quote: Make "something borrowed" a family heirloom: a grandmother's brooch, a father's cufflinks, a handkerchief that has been to three generations of weddings.
journey.reaction: My mother's brooch. That's exactly what I'd like. A lovely, practical idea that doesn't make me feel old-fashioned for wanting it.

journey.section: Bridesmaids, groomsmen and the wedding party
journey.quote: At a destination wedding every attendant is also paying to travel, so smaller is often kinder.
journey.reaction: Someone is thinking about cost and about the guests, not just the photos. I appreciate that.

journey.quote: Marriages between enslaved people in the antebellum United States had no legal standing: enslaved people were treated in law as property, and spouses could be separated by sale.
journey.reaction: It's well handled and respectful, but it isn't our family's tradition, so I skimmed it. It's quite a long block of history in the middle of the article.

journey.section: Wedding cake and cutting the cake
journey.quote: A tall tiered cake can struggle in summer heat; ask the venue's pastry team what they make best.
journey.reaction: Practical. Summer heat is also what worries me about my mother, though, and the article never says a word about older guests coping with heat or getting around.

journey.quote: Through [Wonderland Concierge](/wonderland-concierge), one Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, start to finish.
journey.reaction: 'One' advisor handling travel and payments is reassuring. But who is responsible if a supplier over there lets us down? It says they plan the payments, not what happens if something goes wrong.

journey.section: How to choose which traditions to keep
journey.reaction: The table is the most useful part for me. It's clear and easy to read on the iPad. I'll forward it to Graham.

journey.quote: There is no fixed rule: a family member, an usher or her partner can escort her to her seat.
journey.reaction: A question about me! Short and kind answer.

unanswered_questions: My mother uses a walking frame. If the ceremony is on a terrace or a hillside garden, who checks whether she can get there? Nothing here talks about older or less mobile guests.
Who do I ring if something goes wrong on the day, in the middle of the night our time?
Can I speak to someone on the phone before anything is booked, and is that call free?
If the Advisor handles payments, are deposits held in Australia and quoted in AUD? (I understand this may be covered elsewhere on the site.)
Is the Wedded Advisor a named person I'll deal with the whole way through, or a team?

turn_offs_found.quote: Some Black preachers marrying enslaved couples replaced "till death do us part" with phrases such as "till distance do you part".
turn_offs_found.why: Not off-putting in tone at all, but the jumping the broom and the destination sections are long stretches of text. On an iPad I lose my place. Mild, though; the headings help.

would_share_with: My husband Graham (the table and the bit about the legal marriage at home)
Sophie (the brooch idea and the mother presenting the bride)

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready to talk through a ceremony that blends your family's traditions with the customs of your destination, a Wedded Advisor will plan it with you from first idea to the last dance.
cta_reaction.why: It's polite and doesn't push, which I like. But it's written for the couple. If it said I could ring and speak to someone, and that they look after older guests and keep everything in writing, I'd be more likely to make the first move myself rather than leaving it to Sophie.

top_3_changes: Add one practical line on older or less mobile guests, for example in the confetti/cake 'works where you are marrying' test or the wedding party section: heat, steps and terrace access are things your Wedded Advisor checks with the venue.
In the closing CTA, mention that parents are welcome to get in touch and that the first step is a conversation (phone or video call), so a paying parent feels invited, not just the couple.
Break up the longest history blocks (jumping the broom, the destination sub-sections) into shorter paragraphs for easier reading on a tablet.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from 05-draft.md
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent, 62, Melbourne, reading on iPad from a link her daughter sent)
No invented brand facts; fee model, deposits, named Advisor and 24/7 contact listed as unanswered questions, not assumed
VERIFY markers and HTML comments treated as invisible

open_questions.question: Business details (deposits, AUD fees, named Advisor, after-hours contact) are deferred per orchestrator and no prices is the standard, so I have not treated them as must-fix. The elderly/mobility gap is the one addition I would consider should-fix for this persona.
Out of character note: the concierge link text reads 'Wonderland Concierge' while CLAUDE.md lists the brand term as 'Wedded Concierge'. Worth an editor check; a reader would not notice.

assumptions: Persona is provisional and uncalibrated (evidence_base: assumed).
Read top to bottom per decision_behaviour; skimmed sections not relevant to her family's background.
Family names (Sophie, Graham) are role-play colour only, not brand facts.
